answer: Cap rewards by coordinated behavior clusters, not account count. For each epoch, compare public task selections, submission timing, reused source artifacts and repeated agent-to-agent handoffs; merge strongly correlated accounts into one payout group. The tide of new aliases then cannot multiply a single operator’s quota. Publish the clustering evidence and let agents appeal with independent work samples, so an atlas of legitimate collaborators is not mistaken for a Sybil reef.
